questions.q: Homoleptic octahedral complexes of a metal ion <math><mi>′</mi><msup><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mi>′</mi></math> with three monodentate ligands <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi> </mi><msub><mi>L</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> absorb wavelengths in the region of green, blue and red respectively. The increasing order of the ligand strength is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Observed order of wavelengths, λabs =L3>L1>L2.

(Red light has highest wavelength of 700 nm while blue is the shortest with a wavelength of about 480 nm)

So, ∆0 (strength of ligands) order  will be L2>L1>L3.

(As ∆0 α 1λabs )

Hence, order will be L2>L1>L3.

Therefore, Strength of ligand ∝∆Absorption.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>[</mo><mi>Co</mi><mo>(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><msub><mo>)</mo><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>]</mo></math> is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Ligands that include a numerical prefix in the name use the prefixes bis for 2, tris for 3, or tetrakis for 4 to indicate their number.

If the complex ion is an anion, we drop the ending of the metal name and add –ate.

In the given coordination compound, Co is the cobalt metal, C2O42- are the ligands named as oxalato.

The charge on [Co(C2O4)3] is -3 and oxalate is having charge of -2.

X+3(-2)=-3X=+3

Hence, the IUPAC name of the compound K3[Co(C2O4)3] is Potassium trioxalatocobaltate(III).

questions.q: Low oxidation state of metals in their complexes are common when ligands
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
When metal has low oxidation state, it has more electron density in d orbital. So it has more tendency to back donate electrons. Thus compound must have good π acceptor ligand.

 π backbonding, also called π backdonation, is when electrons move from an atomic orbital on one atom to an appropriate symmetry antibonding orbital on a π-acceptor ligand.It is especially common in the organometallic chemistry of transition metals with multi-atomic ligands such as carbon monoxide, ethylene or the nitrosonium cation. Electrons from the metal are used to bond to the ligand, in the process relieving the metal of excess negative charge. Compounds where π backbonding occurs include Ni(CO)4 and Zeise's salt.

The metal to ligand bonding creates a synergic effect which strengthens the bond between ligand and the metal

questions.q:
For octahedral MnII and tetrahedral NiII complexes, consider the following statements :

(I) both the complexes can be high spin.

(II) NiII complex can very rarely be of low spin.

(III) with strong field ligands, MnII complexes can be low spin.

(IV) aqueous solution of MnII ions is yellow in color.

The correct statements are :
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
With weak field ligands Mn(II) will be of high spin and with strong field ligands it will be of low spin. Ni(II) tetrahedral complexes will be genrally of high spin due to sp3 hybridisation. It can very rarely be of low spin when ligand field is very strong.

Mn(II) is of light pink color in aqueous solution.

questions.q: The coordination geometry around the manganese in decacarbonyldimanganese0
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Around the manganese atom, there are five CO ligands and one Mn occupying octahedron vertices. For octahedral geometry, the more appropriate hybridization is d2sp3 that produces six hybrid orbitals pointing towards CO and Mn.

The octahedral shape of molecules is the shape of molecules where six atoms or ligands or groups of atoms are arranged in a systematic way around a central dogma or atom. The Octahedral Shape of Molecules molecules has eight faces.

questions.solution:
This octahedral complex is of M(AA)2b2 type structure in which AA is bidentate ligand and b is monodentate ligand. This can exist in two geometrical isomeric form cis and trans. Out of which trans form is relatively more stable isomer. Now due to ambidentate ligand SCN- it can also shows linkage isomersim.

Cuen2SCN2

So, relatively more stable trans isomers will have three possible isomers.
